title: Narendra Modi
subtitle: From RSS pracharak to three-term Prime Minister · 1950 –
subject: narendra-modi
intro: Born into a modest family in Vadnagar, Gujarat, Narendra Modi joined the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh as a boy and spent two decades as one of its full-time organisers before the RSS lent him to the Bharatiya Janata Party. He became Chief Minister of Gujarat in 2001 and months later the state was engulfed by the 2002 riots, which shaped his reputation at home and abroad for a decade. Re-elected three times on a record of investment and growth, he led the BJP to the first single-party majority in thirty years in 2014 and has been Prime Minister since — through demonetisation and the GST, the revocation of Article 370, the pandemic, and confrontations with Pakistan and China. Supporters credit him with welfare delivery, infrastructure and a larger global role for India; critics point to majoritarian politics, the treatment of minorities, and pressure on the press and institutions.

events.title: Born at Vadnagar
events.summary: Narendra Damodardas Modi is born in Vadnagar, in the Mehsana district of what was then Bombay State, the third of six children of Damodardas Modi and Hiraben. The family belong to the Ghanchi community of oil-pressers, an Other Backward Class.

events.title: Joins the RSS shakha
events.summary: At about eight Modi begins attending the local shakha of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. By his own account he also helps his father sell tea at Vadnagar railway station as a boy.

events.title: Gujarat becomes a state
events.summary: Bombay State is split on linguistic lines into Maharashtra and Gujarat; Vadnagar is now in Gujarat.

events.title: Marriage and leaving home
events.summary: Betrothed as a child under his community's custom, Modi is married to Jashodaben at about eighteen but soon leaves home. The couple never live together, and he does not publicly acknowledge the marriage until his 2014 election nomination papers.

events.title: Two years of travel
events.summary: After leaving school Modi travels for about two years — by his account to Ramakrishna Mission ashrams and through the Himalayas — before returning to Gujarat and settling in Ahmedabad.

events.title: Full-time RSS pracharak
events.summary: Modi becomes a full-time worker (pracharak) of the RSS, based at its Gujarat headquarters in Ahmedabad. He will spend the next fourteen years as an organiser for the Sangh.

events.title: Underground in the Emergency
events.summary: When Indira Gandhi declares the Emergency, suspending civil liberties and banning the RSS, Modi goes underground in Gujarat, moving in disguise and helping circulate banned literature. He later writes a Gujarati book about the period, Sangharsh Ma Gujarat.

events.title: Lent to the BJP
events.summary: The RSS assigns Modi to its political ally, the Bharatiya Janata Party. In 1987 he helps run the BJP's winning campaign for the Ahmedabad municipal corporation and becomes the party's organising secretary in Gujarat.

events.title: Advani's Ram Rath Yatra
events.summary: L. K. Advani sets out from Somnath on the Ram Rath Yatra, a procession to Ayodhya to campaign for a Ram temple on the site of the Babri Masjid. Modi organises the Gujarat leg. Advani is arrested in Bihar before reaching Ayodhya.

events.title: Ekta Yatra to Srinagar
events.summary: Modi organises Murli Manohar Joshi's Ekta Yatra from Kanyakumari to Srinagar, which ends with the two hoisting the national flag at Lal Chowk on Republic Day amid the Kashmir insurgency.

events.title: Babri Masjid demolished
events.summary: Kar sevaks tear down the sixteenth-century Babri Masjid at Ayodhya; the riots that follow across India kill some two thousand people.

events.title: Moved to Delhi
events.summary: The BJP wins its first majority in Gujarat in 1995 under Keshubhai Patel, but a revolt by Shankersinh Vaghela splits the party. Modi, a central figure in the feud, is moved to Delhi as a national secretary of the BJP, working on the party organisation in Haryana and Himachal Pradesh.

events.title: BJP general secretary
events.summary: Modi is promoted to general secretary (organisation) of the BJP, the party's key link to the RSS, as Atal Bihari Vajpayee becomes Prime Minister.

events.title: Gujarat earthquake
events.summary: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake centred near Bhuj kills some 20,000 people. Criticism of the relief effort and by-election defeats weaken Keshubhai Patel's government.

events.title: Chief Minister of Gujarat
events.summary: The BJP leadership replaces Keshubhai Patel with Modi, who has never contested an election, as Chief Minister of Gujarat.

events.title: Wins Rajkot by-election
events.summary: Modi enters the Gujarat assembly by winning a by-election in Rajkot II.

events.title: Godhra train burning
events.summary: A coach of the Sabarmati Express carrying kar sevaks back from Ayodhya is set on fire at Godhra station, killing 59 people. A state-appointed commission later calls it a conspiracy and a special court convicts 31 people in 2011; a committee set up by the railway ministry had called it an accident.

events.title: The 2002 Gujarat riots
events.summary: Mobs attack Muslims across Gujarat for weeks; in the Gulbarg Society massacre and the Naroda Patiya massacre alone some 160 people are killed. Official figures put the dead at 1,044 — 790 Muslims and 254 Hindus — with others missing; independent estimates run up to 2,000. Modi's government is accused of failing to stop the violence, or of complicity, which it denies.

events.title: "Follow raj dharma"
events.summary: At a press conference in Ahmedabad Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee publicly tells Modi to follow raj dharma — a ruler's duty to treat all subjects equally. Modi offers to resign at a BJP meeting in Goa days later; the party rejects it.

events.title: Wins Gujarat election
events.summary: After dissolving the assembly early, Modi campaigns across the state and the BJP wins 127 of 182 seats.

events.title: First Vibrant Gujarat summit
events.summary: Modi launches a biennial investors' summit, Vibrant Gujarat, which becomes the centrepiece of his pitch of Gujarat as a business-friendly, fast-growing state.

events.title: US revokes his visa
events.summary: The United States revokes Modi's visa under a law barring officials responsible for severe violations of religious freedom. Britain and the European Union also keep their distance until 2012–13.

events.title: Re-elected in Gujarat
events.summary: The BJP wins 117 seats and Modi begins a third term as Chief Minister.

events.title: Tata Nano comes to Sanand
events.summary: After protests over land acquisition drive Tata Motors out of Singur in West Bengal, Ratan Tata announces that the Nano car plant will be built at Sanand in Gujarat — reportedly after a one-word text from Modi: "Suswagatam" (welcome).

events.title: SIT finds no case against him
events.summary: A Special Investigation Team appointed by the Supreme Court, which questioned Modi in 2010, files a closure report finding no prosecutable evidence against him over the riots. Zakia Jafri, whose husband was killed at Gulbarg Society, challenges it; the Supreme Court finally dismisses her plea in 2022.

events.title: Former minister convicted
events.summary: Maya Kodnani, who had served as a minister in Modi's government, is sentenced to 28 years for her role in the Naroda Patiya massacre. The Gujarat High Court acquits her in 2018.

events.title: Third straight win in Gujarat
events.summary: The BJP wins 115 seats; Modi's victory speech is delivered in Hindi, aimed at a national audience.

events.title: Named BJP's PM candidate
events.summary: Over the objections of L. K. Advani, the BJP names Modi its candidate for Prime Minister. Amit Shah, his closest aide, runs the campaign in Uttar Pradesh.

events.title: BJP wins a majority
events.summary: The BJP wins 282 of 543 seats — the first single-party majority in the Lok Sabha since 1984 — while the Congress falls to 44. Modi wins both Vadodara and Varanasi and keeps Varanasi.

events.title: Prime Minister of India
events.summary: Modi is sworn in as the 14th Prime Minister at Rashtrapati Bhavan, with the leaders of the SAARC countries, including Pakistan's Nawaz Sharif, in the audience.

events.title: Jan Dhan bank accounts
events.summary: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana sets out to give every household a bank account; within a decade more than 500 million are opened, later used to pay subsidies directly.

events.title: Make in India
events.summary: A campaign to turn India into a manufacturing hub for global companies.

events.title: Madison Square Garden
events.summary: Nine years after being refused a visa, Modi addresses some 19,000 Indian-Americans at Madison Square Garden in New York, the first of many diaspora rallies.

events.title: Swachh Bharat Mission
events.summary: On Gandhi's birthday Modi launches a campaign to end open defecation and clean up India's towns, building more than 100 million household toilets over five years.

events.title: First Mann Ki Baat
events.summary: Modi begins a monthly radio address, Mann Ki Baat ("from the heart"); he gives no regular press conferences.

events.title: NITI Aayog replaces the Planning Commission
events.summary: The Planning Commission, set up under Nehru in 1950 to draw up five-year plans, is replaced by a policy think tank, NITI Aayog.

events.title: Obama at Republic Day
events.summary: Barack Obama is the first US President to be chief guest at the Republic Day parade.

events.title: First International Day of Yoga
events.summary: Proposed by Modi at the United Nations and adopted by the General Assembly, the first International Day of Yoga is marked with a mass session on Rajpath in Delhi.

events.title: Digital India
events.summary: A programme to extend broadband and put government services online. With Aadhaar identity numbers and the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), launched in 2016, it builds the "digital public infrastructure" India later promotes abroad.

events.title: Surprise stop in Lahore
events.summary: Returning from Kabul, Modi makes an unannounced stop in Lahore to wish Nawaz Sharif on his birthday — the first visit to Pakistan by an Indian Prime Minister in over a decade. A week later militants attack the Pathankot air base.

events.title: Ujjwala gas connections
events.summary: A scheme to give poor households free LPG cooking-gas connections, in place of wood and dung fires.

events.title: Uri attack
events.summary: Militants attack an army base at Uri in Kashmir, killing 19 soldiers.

events.title: "Surgical strikes" across the LoC
events.summary: India announces that its special forces have struck militant launch pads across the Line of Control. Pakistan denies the strikes took place.

events.title: Demonetisation
events.summary: In a televised address Modi announces that ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes — about 86% of the cash in circulation — will cease to be legal tender at midnight, to fight black money, counterfeiting and terror financing. Weeks of queues at banks follow; the Reserve Bank later reports that over 99% of the cancelled notes came back.

events.title: Doklam standoff
events.summary: Indian troops block Chinese road-building on the Doklam plateau, claimed by Bhutan; the two armies face off for 73 days before both pull back.

events.title: GST comes into force
events.summary: At a midnight session of Parliament Modi launches the Goods and Services Tax, replacing a tangle of central and state taxes with a single national system — a reform debated since 2000.

events.title: First PM to visit Israel
events.summary: Modi becomes the first Indian Prime Minister to visit Israel, received by Benjamin Netanyahu; he does not stop in Ramallah, breaking with past practice.

events.title: Electoral bonds
events.summary: The government notifies electoral bonds, letting donors give unlimited sums to parties anonymously. The BJP receives the largest share. In 2024 the Supreme Court strikes the scheme down as unconstitutional and orders the donors' names published.

events.title: Ayushman Bharat health insurance
events.summary: Modi launches a government health-insurance scheme covering hospital care up to ₹5 lakh a year for some 100 million poor families.

events.title: Statue of Unity
events.summary: Modi unveils a 182-metre statue of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on the Narmada in Gujarat — the tallest statue in the world — on Patel's birth anniversary.

events.title: Pulwama attack
events.summary: A suicide bomber of the Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed rams a car into a convoy at Pulwama in Kashmir, killing 40 paramilitary police.

events.title: PM-KISAN
events.summary: Weeks before the election, the government begins paying farming families ₹6,000 a year directly into their bank accounts.

events.title: Balakot airstrike
events.summary: Indian jets strike what India says is a militant training camp at Balakot inside Pakistan — the first such strike across the international border since 1971. Next day an Indian pilot, Abhinandan Varthaman, is shot down and captured in a dogfight; Pakistan returns him on 1 March.

events.title: Re-elected with a larger majority
events.summary: The BJP wins 303 seats, the NDA 353, in a campaign dominated by national security after Pulwama and Balakot. Modi is sworn in for a second term on 30 May, with Amit Shah as Home Minister.

events.title: Instant triple talaq made a crime
events.summary: A new law makes instant triple talaq — a Muslim husband divorcing his wife by saying "talaq" three times — a criminal offence, two years after the Supreme Court declared it invalid.
events.wiki: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019

events.title: Article 370 revoked
events.summary: The government ends the special constitutional status of Jammu and Kashmir and splits the state into two union territories, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. Thousands of troops are deployed, the internet is cut for months and political leaders are detained. The Supreme Court upholds the move in December 2023.
events.wiki: Revocation of the special status of Jammu and Kashmir

events.title: "Howdy, Modi!" in Houston
events.summary: Some 50,000 people fill a stadium in Houston, where Modi shares the stage with Donald Trump.

events.title: Supreme Court's Ayodhya verdict
events.summary: A unanimous Supreme Court gives the disputed site at Ayodhya to a trust to build a Ram temple, while ruling that the 1992 demolition of the mosque was illegal and allotting five acres elsewhere for a new mosque.

events.title: Citizenship (Amendment) Act
events.summary: Parliament offers fast-track citizenship to Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi and Christian migrants from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan — but not Muslims. Protests break out across the country, including a months-long sit-in at Shaheen Bagh in Delhi. Its rules are notified only in March 2024.

events.title: Delhi riots
events.summary: As Donald Trump visits India, clashes between supporters and opponents of the CAA in north-east Delhi turn into riots that kill 53 people, most of them Muslims.

events.title: National lockdown
events.summary: With four hours' notice Modi orders 1.3 billion people to stay home for 21 days to slow COVID-19. Millions of migrant workers, suddenly without work, set off on foot for their villages. The lockdown is extended into June.

events.title: Atmanirbhar Bharat
events.summary: Modi announces a ₹20 lakh crore relief package under the slogan Atmanirbhar Bharat — "self-reliant India".

events.title: Galwan Valley clash
events.summary: Indian and Chinese soldiers fight with clubs and stones in the Galwan Valley in Ladakh — the first deadly clash on the border since 1975. Twenty Indian soldiers are killed; China later admits four deaths. India bans dozens of Chinese apps, including TikTok.

events.title: Lays the Ram temple foundation
events.summary: Modi performs the bhoomi pujan for the Ram temple at Ayodhya.

events.title: Farm laws
events.summary: Three laws opening agricultural markets to private traders are passed by voice vote in the Rajya Sabha amid uproar.

events.title: Farmers camp at Delhi's borders
events.summary: Tens of thousands of farmers, mostly from Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, camp on the highways into Delhi for more than a year. On 19 November 2021 Modi announces the farm laws will be repealed.

events.title: Vaccination begins
events.summary: India begins vaccinating against COVID-19 with Covishield and the home-grown Covaxin. It passes one billion doses on 21 October 2021.

events.title: The second COVID wave
events.summary: The Delta variant drives cases above 400,000 a day; hospitals run out of oxygen and crematoria are overwhelmed. Official figures record about 480,000 COVID deaths by early 2022; the WHO estimates some 4.7 million excess deaths in 2020–21, a figure the government rejects.

events.title: His mother dies
events.summary: Modi's mother Hiraben dies in Ahmedabad aged 99; he carries her bier at the funeral in Gandhinagar.

events.title: New Parliament building
events.summary: Modi inaugurates a new Parliament building in New Delhi, part of the redevelopment of the Central Vista. Twenty opposition parties boycott the ceremony.

events.title: State visit to Washington
events.summary: On a state visit to the United States Modi addresses a joint session of Congress for the second time — and takes a rare question from a reporter about the treatment of minorities.

events.title: Chandrayaan-3 lands on the Moon
events.summary: India becomes the fourth country to land on the Moon, and the first near its south pole. Modi watches the landing live from the BRICS summit in Johannesburg.

events.title: G20 summit in New Delhi
events.summary: India hosts the G20 at the new Bharat Mandapam. Despite divisions over Ukraine the summit agrees a joint declaration, and the African Union is admitted as a permanent member.

events.title: Women's reservation act
events.summary: In the first session in the new building Parliament reserves one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies for women — to take effect after the next census and redrawing of constituencies.

events.title: Ram temple consecrated
events.summary: Modi leads the consecration (pran pratishtha) of the idol of Ram Lalla at the new temple in Ayodhya, on the site where the Babri Masjid stood — the fulfilment of a campaign he had helped organise since 1990.

events.title: Electoral bonds struck down
events.summary: A five-judge bench of the Supreme Court unanimously strikes down electoral bonds, saying voters have a right to know who funds parties.

events.title: Third term, without a majority
events.summary: The BJP falls to 240 seats, short of a majority for the first time under Modi, and loses heavily in Uttar Pradesh, including Faizabad, the seat that takes in Ayodhya. With N. Chandrababu Naidu's TDP and Nitish Kumar's JD(U) the NDA has 293. Sworn in on 9 June, Modi equals Nehru's record of three consecutive terms.

events.title: Moscow, then Kyiv
events.summary: Modi meets Vladimir Putin in Moscow in July and, six weeks later, Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv — the first visit to independent Ukraine by an Indian Prime Minister — telling both that "this is not an era of war". India keeps buying discounted Russian oil.

events.title: Pahalgam attack
events.summary: Gunmen kill 26 people, almost all of them tourists, in a meadow near Pahalgam in Kashmir. The next day India suspends the Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan.

events.title: Operation Sindoor
events.summary: India strikes nine sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir that it links to militant groups. Four days of missile, drone and artillery exchanges follow — the most serious fighting between the two nuclear-armed neighbours in decades — until a ceasefire on 10 May. Donald Trump claims credit for it; India says it was agreed directly between the two militaries.

events.title: Passes Indira Gandhi
events.summary: With 4,078 days in office Modi passes Indira Gandhi's unbroken tenure to become the second-longest continuously serving Prime Minister, after Nehru.

events.title: Trump's 50% tariffs
events.summary: The United States doubles its tariff on most Indian goods to 50%, adding a penalty for India's purchases of Russian oil — the sharpest strain in India–US relations in decades.

events.title: In China for the SCO
events.summary: Modi visits China for the first time in seven years for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit at Tianjin, meeting Xi Jinping and, warmly, Vladimir Putin.

events.title: GST simplified
events.summary: Most goods move to two GST rates, 5% and 18%, with a higher rate for luxury and "sin" goods — cutting taxes on many everyday items, as promised in Modi's Independence Day speech.

events.title: NDA sweeps Bihar
events.summary: The NDA wins over 200 of Bihar's 243 seats, with the BJP the largest party, and Nitish Kumar stays Chief Minister.
